  "schema_version": "evidence_intent_extraction_v1",

  "draft_intents": [
    {
      "draft_id": "D0001",
      "locator": "page 52",
      "start_segment_id": "S00001",
      "end_segment_id": "S00001",
      "intent": "IMF tabular estimates place Mexico's 2022 current-account deficit at 1.2 percent of GDP, compared with a 0.4 percent deficit in 2021 and a 2.5 percent surplus in 2020.",
      "attribution": "IMF staff estimates drawing on the Bank of Mexico and Mexico's National Institute of Statistics and Geography",
      "period_fit": "Direct 2022 estimate with 2020–2021 comparator years.",
      "limitations": "A national macroeconomic outcome; the passage does not identify a specific decision by the ruler or establish ruler-level causation.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.7", "5B.9", "5B.10", "8B.7"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0002",
      "locator": "page 53",
      "start_segment_id": "S00001",
      "end_segment_id": "S00001",
      "intent": "Mexico's regulatory-capital-to-risk-weighted-assets ratio was 18.7 percent in the second quarter of 2022, down from 19.5 percent in 2021 but above its 16.0 percent level in 2019.",
      "attribution": "Mexican authorities and IMF Financial Soundness Indicators",
      "period_fit": "Direct observation for 2022Q2 with historical comparators.",
      "limitations": "The indicator describes banking-system capitalization and does not by itself identify a ruler decision, implementation mechanism, or causal contribution.",
      "polarity": "positive",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.7", "5B.9", "5B.10", "8B.7"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0003",
      "locator": "page 54",
      "start_segment_id": "S00005",
      "end_segment_id": "S00005",
      "intent": "Nonperforming loans held by Mexican deposit-taking institutions equaled 2.3 percent of total gross loans in June 2022, compared with 2.0 percent in 2021 and 2.4 percent in 2020.",
      "attribution": "IMF table based on Mexican official sources and Fund staff estimates",
      "period_fit": "Direct June 2022 observation with 2020–2021 comparators.",
      "limitations": "This is a financial-system condition, not evidence of a particular ruler action or causal effect.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.7", "5B.9", "5B.10", "8B.7"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0004",
      "locator": "page 55",
      "start_segment_id": "S00001",
      "end_segment_id": "S00001",
      "intent": "IMF staff projected real GDP growth of 2.1 percent for Mexico in 2022, following an 8.1 percent contraction in 2020 and 4.8 percent growth in 2021.",
      "attribution": "IMF staff projections drawing on Mexican official sources",
      "period_fit": "Direct 2022 projection with pandemic-period comparators.",
      "limitations": "A projection rather than a realized full-year outcome; it does not isolate policy effects from reopening, baseline effects, or external conditions.",
      "polarity": "positive",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.9", "5B.10", "6B.10", "8B.7", "8B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0005",
      "locator": "page 56",
      "start_segment_id": "S00012",
      "end_segment_id": "S00012",
      "intent": "Bank credit to Mexico's nonfinancial private sector was projected to grow by 10.7 percent in 2022, while declining to 26.5 percent of GDP from 26.7 percent in 2021 and 28.6 percent in 2020.",
      "attribution": "Bank of Mexico, Mexico's National Institute of Statistics and Geography, and IMF staff estimates",
      "period_fit": "Direct 2022 projection with 2020–2021 comparators.",
      "limitations": "The nominal growth rate may partly reflect inflation, and the source does not attribute the change to ruler policy.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.4", "5B.7", "5B.9", "5B.10", "8B.7"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0006",
      "locator": "page 57",
      "start_segment_id": "S00001",
      "end_segment_id": "S00004",
      "intent": "IMF staff assessed Mexico's 2021 external position as broadly consistent with medium-term fundamentals and desirable policies, attributing its rebalancing to domestic and foreign economic reopening and recovery and to a narrower cross-country fiscal-policy gap; staff expected the current-account deficit to stabilize near 1 percent of GDP over the medium term.",
      "attribution": "IMF staff external-sector assessment",
      "period_fit": "Retrospective assessment of 2021 published in the 2022 report, with a medium-term projection.",
      "limitations": "The assessment is country-level, partly model-based, and does not allocate responsibility between the ruler, independent institutions, external recovery, or foreign fiscal developments.",
      "polarity": "positive",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.7", "5B.10", "8B.7", "8B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0007",
      "locator": "page 57",
      "start_segment_id": "S00005",
      "end_segment_id": "S00007",
      "intent": "IMF staff judged further structural reforms critical for medium- and long-term growth, exports, and external sustainability, specifically identifying economic informality, governance gaps, private-sector participation in energy, and Pemex's business strategy and governance as areas requiring action.",
      "attribution": "IMF staff policy recommendation",
      "period_fit": "Contemporaneous 2022 assessment of unresolved policy needs and prospective reforms.",
      "limitations": "A recommendation rather than evidence that the ruler adopted or implemented the reforms; it signals outstanding constraints but does not independently establish responsibility.",
      "polarity": "negative",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.1", "5B.3", "5B.4", "5B.5", "5B.6", "5B.7", "5B.10", "8B.2", "8B.6", "8B.8", "8B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0008",
      "locator": "page 57",
      "start_segment_id": "S00020",
      "end_segment_id": "S00025",
      "intent": "IMF staff projected Mexico's 2022 current-account deficit to widen to about 1 percent of GDP because higher global commodity prices affected Mexico as a net commodity importer; staff expected direct trade effects from the war in Ukraine to be small because trade links with Russia and eastern Europe were limited, while the domestic fuel-price ceiling and associated subsidies would weaken substitution and income responses to higher oil prices and amplify the current-account impact.",
      "attribution": "IMF staff external-sector assessment",
      "period_fit": "Direct 2022 projection and policy-mechanism assessment.",
      "limitations": "The forecast carried considerable uncertainty from the COVID-19 pandemic and the war in Ukraine; the passage identifies a policy mechanism but does not state who personally authorized it.",
      "polarity": "negative",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.1", "5B.3", "5B.9", "5B.10", "6B.6", "8B.2", "8B.6", "8B.7", "8B.9"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0009",
      "locator": "page 57",
      "start_segment_id": "S00042",
      "end_segment_id": "S00044",
      "intent": "Mexico's central bank maintained a free-floating exchange-rate policy with discretionary intervention reserved for disorderly market conditions; it conducted no foreign-exchange intervention in 2021, while gross reserves rose from USD 199 billion at end-2020 to USD 208 billion at end-2021, largely because of the IMF's general SDR allocation.",
      "attribution": "IMF staff description of central-bank policy and reserve developments",
      "period_fit": "Retrospective 2021 institutional evidence included in the 2022 report.",
      "limitations": "The central bank is institutionally distinct from the ruler, and most of the reserve increase is attributed to an external IMF allocation rather than executive policy.",
      "polarity": "positive",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.2", "5B.3", "5B.9", "5B.10", "8B.3", "8B.5", "8B.6", "8B.7"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0010",
      "locator": "page 58",
      "start_segment_id": "S00004",
      "end_segment_id": "S00007",
      "intent": "IMF staff assessed systemic social unrest as a medium-likelihood but high-impact risk for Mexico, with pressure on basic-goods prices potentially causing tension; recommended responses included tighter monetary policy, larger and better-targeted social transfers for vulnerable households, and accelerated investment in low-income regions.",
      "attribution": "IMF staff Risk Assessment Matrix",
      "period_fit": "Contemporaneous risk assessment and prospective policy advice at the time of the 2022 consultations.",
      "limitations": "The risk classification is a subjective staff assessment, and the listed measures are recommendations rather than actions shown to have been implemented.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["3B.6", "3B.9", "3B.10", "5B.8", "5B.9", "6B.3", "6B.6", "6B.10", "8B.8", "8B.9"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0011",
      "locator": "page 59",
      "start_segment_id": "S00001",
      "end_segment_id": "S00004",
      "intent": "IMF staff treated renewed local COVID-19 outbreaks as a medium risk that could reverse declines in hospitalizations and deaths and renew supply constraints; recommended responses included restarting vaccination, obtaining variant boosters when available, considering renewed support for key industries, and expanding targeted transfers for the most vulnerable.",
      "attribution": "IMF staff Risk Assessment Matrix",
      "period_fit": "Contemporaneous 2022 risk assessment and prospective recommendations.",
      "limitations": "The passage describes a scenario and recommended response, not verified implementation or outcomes; some effects would depend on variants, trading-partner restrictions, and vaccine availability.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["3B.7", "3B.9", "3B.10", "5B.9", "6B.2", "6B.3", "6B.6", "6B.10", "8B.8", "8B.9"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0012",
      "locator": "page 60",
      "start_segment_id": "S00002",
      "end_segment_id": "S00005",
      "intent": "IMF staff judged Mexico's overall sovereign-stress risk to be moderate: deteriorating global conditions were expected to slow the post-pandemic recovery in 2023 and leave debt elevated and not stabilized by 2027, while trend growth and a tight fiscal stance were expected to contain the debt path over ten years; the balanced-budget rule helped contain debt but often restrained investment and developmental expenditure.",
      "attribution": "IMF staff sovereign-risk and debt-sustainability analysis",
      "period_fit": "Forward-looking assessment produced in 2022, with implications for 2023–2027 and an extended ten-year horizon.",
      "limitations": "A projection and institutional assessment rather than a realized outcome; global conditions are an explicit external constraint, and the passage does not assign the fiscal framework exclusively to the incumbent ruler.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.1", "5B.3", "5B.6", "5B.9", "5B.10", "6B.1", "6B.2", "6B.9", "6B.10", "8B.6", "8B.7", "8B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0013",
      "locator": "page 61",
      "start_segment_id": "S00007",
      "end_segment_id": "S00011",
      "intent": "IMF staff reported that Mexico's debt-sustainability coverage excluded state and local governments because of their limited debt-carrying capacity and the absence of a federal legal obligation to guarantee or assume their debt; staff were unaware of data on accounts payable, and debt was not consolidated across the federal government and nonfinancial public sector.",
      "attribution": "IMF staff commentary on debt coverage and disclosure",
      "period_fit": "Contemporaneous disclosure limitation documented in the 2022 assessment.",
      "limitations": "The exclusions partly reflect Mexico's federal legal structure, and the missing-payables statement is a staff data-availability limitation rather than proof that the underlying information did not exist.",
      "polarity": "negative",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.7", "5B.10", "7B.6", "7B.7", "7B.10", "8B.3", "8B.5", "8B.7", "8B.10"]
    }
  ],
